prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. He opened every crate rather than a sample, counted its contents against the ship's papers, and listed even the smallest difference, down to a missing spoon or a bolt of cloth a yard short. Captains complained that unloading at his port took twice as long as at the larger ports on the river, and his successor found the reports accurate to the last item. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He checked every crate item by item and recorded the slightest discrepancy, so he was "meticulous." "Naive" fails because he trusted nothing on the ship's papers without counting it himself; "lenient" fails because the passage reports how closely he checked, not how mildly he punished; "incorruptible" fails because nothing concerns bribes or attempts to sway him.

naive.quote: counted its contents against the ship's papers
naive.why: he verified every declaration rather than accepting it

lenient.why: the passage is about the thoroughness of his checking, not about mild treatment of offenders

incorruptible.why: his distinction is precision; no one is said to have tried to buy him

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. His reports show him finding smuggled tobacco or brandy in the crates of about one ship in ten, close to the rate at the larger ports on the river. He fined captains caught for the first time a few shillings, far below what the law allowed, and let those who admitted the offense keep their goods once they had paid the duty. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He caught smugglers as often as other ports did but punished them far more mildly than the law allowed, so he was "lenient." "Naive" fails because he found smuggled goods at the normal rate and so was not being fooled; "meticulous" fails because his catch rate was merely ordinary and nothing shows unusual thoroughness; "incorruptible" fails because the passage concerns his penalties, not any refusal of bribes.

naive.quote: close to the rate at the larger ports
naive.why: he detected smuggling as well as other inspectors, so he was not being taken in

meticulous.why: an ordinary detection rate shows ordinary care, not exceptional precision

incorruptible.quote: far below what the law allowed
incorruptible.why: what distinguishes him is mild penalties, not resistance to bribery

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. He took each captain's word for what the crates held, and smugglers soon learned to mark crates of brandy as machine parts and crates of tobacco as books. His reports record almost no seizures in twenty-three years, and two captains later wrote in their memoirs of how easily his port could be worked. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He believed what captains told him, and smugglers exploited that trust with false labels, so he was "naive." "Meticulous" fails because he did not check the crates against their labels; "lenient" fails because he caught almost no one and so had no one to treat mildly; "incorruptible" fails because smugglers did not need to buy him: they simply deceived him.

meticulous.why: he accepted declarations instead of examining the goods

lenient.quote: almost no seizures in twenty-three years
lenient.why: leniency requires catching offenders and punishing them lightly; he caught almost none

incorruptible.quote: how easily his port could be worked
incorruptible.why: the smugglers got through by deception, so his honesty toward bribes is never at issue

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. Merchants' letters complain that the gifts of wine and banknotes that eased crates through other ports on the river came back to them from his, and he sent each such offer, with the giver's name, to his superiors. Several captains who had made offers were prosecuted on his reports. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He returned the gifts that bought easy passage elsewhere and reported those who offered them, so he was "incorruptible." "Lenient" fails because he turned the givers over for prosecution; "naive" fails because he recognized the gifts for what they were; "meticulous" fails because the passage concerns his refusal of bribes, not the thoroughness of his inspections.

lenient.why: he had offenders prosecuted, the reverse of letting them off lightly

naive.quote: with the giver's name, to his superiors
naive.why: reporting the gifts as offers shows he understood exactly what they were

meticulous.why: what sets him apart from other ports is his refusal of payment, not careful counting
